title: Generous Dealing of Yahya Son of Khalid with a Man Who Forged a Letter in His Name
logline: A penniless man forges a letter from the vizier Yahya to Yahya's old enemy, the governor of Armenia. Instead of exposing him, Yahya owns the letter to end the feud, and the forger goes home with two fortunes.
moral: A generous man turns even a wrong done to him into a chance for peace; mercy repaired what pride had broken.
tone: Light comic suspense: a small bluffer in over his head, a proud governor, and a wise vizier who is always one step ahead. Warm, never cruel; the threat stays a picture in a box.

beats.summary: A poor man of Iraq with an empty purse wants a way out.
He hears of the old quarrel between Governor Abdullah and the vizier Yahya.
He forges a letter in the name of Yahya asking that its bearer be honoured.
After a long road he hands it to Abdullah with a bold face.
Abdullah doubts: why would his enemy write to him?
The bargain: true means reward, false means severe punishment.
An envoy rides to Baghdad to ask Yahya himself.
Days of dread: wealth or a beating.
Yahya sees at once the letter is not in his hand.
He chooses peace and says it is truly his.
Abdullah, delighted, pours gifts on the man: 200,000 dirhams, ten horses, chests, servants, jewels.
The name that caused the quarrel now renews the friendship.
Back in Baghdad he confesses to Yahya and thanks him.
He offers a share; Yahya smiles and refuses.
You were the cause of peace between two parted friends.
Yahya doubles the gifts; the poor man leaves with two fortunes.

sets.description: The poor man's one-room hut in cutaway, palette 'day': walls x 110..890, hanging empty jar on the hook, shelf, stool, window right, door left. A plank table (120 x 14 on two blocks, top y 800) is drawn by the scene for the writing.

Strip w 2400 for the three journeys. Armenia is the right end: a walled town gate plus three snow-capped triangle mountains drawn by the scene behind the far dunes (grey with white caps, heights 260..340). Baghdad is the left end: far city silhouette with domes. Travel to Armenia goes left to right; travel to Baghdad right to left, always.

Abdullah's hall in Armenia: variant 'palace', wall 'blue', door arch left (x 40..250, top y 480) with outside(ctx) used for the sky cycle and the horses, dais x 560..900 top y 860 with throne, red carpet runner, two lamps, one stool at x 300. Anchors from the returned object.

Yahya's hall in Baghdad: the same set function with wall 'ochre', cushions on the dais, window with a light shaft, a low desk with papers. The different wall colour and the navy vizier tell the two halls apart at a glance.

Baghdad street outside Yahya's palace for the ending: palette 'clear', w 1400, palace facade at the right with the door open (palaceDoor 1) and the balcony; two closed stalls and a few props at the left so the procession reads against plain wall.

props.description: The letter (planned 'scroll'): paper rectangle 70 x 100 at hand size with rolled ends, wavy ink lines (lines 0..1 draw-on), roll 0..1, a wax seal disc r 14 (red for the forgery, yellow for Yahya's true reply), optional header medallion. Insert size 300 x 420.
Quill (feather 60 long, white with a blue edge, black nib) and a squat inkpot 30 x 26 with a black ellipse of ink.
Planned 'bindle': a knotted cloth bundle (r 30, red with white dots) on a stick 120 long, carried over the shoulder.
Planned 'coinPile': a mound of yellow coins, n grows from 0 to full (mound 160 x 90 at full), single coins can fall and hop.
Chest from the planned 'treasureHoard' module: 130 x 90 box, curved lid with open 0..1, yellow bands; contents option 'cloth' (three folded bolts red, blue, yellow) or 'coins'.
Planned 'jewels (with jewelBox)': casket 60 x 40 with a hinged lid and four cut gems; used with goldGlow.
Planned 'hourglass': panel-space time meter 60 x 100 with level 0..1 and a flip.

subtitles.ar: كان رجل فقير من العراق|يبحث عن وسيلة يخرج بها من ضيق العيش.|سمع عن والي أرمينية عبد الله بن مالك،|وعن خلاف قديم بينه وبين الوزير يحيى بن خالد البرمكي.
subtitles.en: A poor Iraqi man|sought a way out of hardship.|He heard of Abdullah ibn Malik, governor of Armenia,|and his long-standing quarrel with Yahya al-Barmaki.

subtitles.ar: كتب الرجل رسالة مزورة،|وجعلها كأنها من يحيى إلى الوالي، يطلب فيها إكرام حاملها ومساعدته.|ثم سافر مسافة طويلة،|ودخل على عبد الله وقدم إليه الرسالة بثقة.
subtitles.en: The man forged a letter|supposedly from Yahya requesting help for its bearer.|After a long journey,|he presented it confidently to Governor Abdullah.

subtitles.ar: قرأ عبد الله الخطاب، وشك في صحته،|لأنه يعرف الخصومة التي بينه وبين يحيى.|قال للرجل: إن كانت الرسالة صحيحة أكرمتك،|وإن كانت كذبًا فلك عقاب شديد.
subtitles.en: Abdullah doubted the letter|because of his feud with Yahya.|He promised a great reward if it was genuine,|but severe punishment if it was false.

subtitles.ar: أقام الرجل عند الوالي ينتظر النتيجة،|بينما أرسل عبد الله رسولًا إلى بغداد ليسأل يحيى بنفسه.|مرت الأيام ثقيلة على الرجل؛|فالجواب قد يجلب له ثروة، أو يعرضه للضرب والإهانة.
subtitles.en: The man waited|while Abdullah sent an envoy to Baghdad.|Each day felt long:|Yahya’s answer could bring him wealth or expose him to a humiliating beating.

subtitles.ar: فهم يحيى الأمر حين قرأ الرسالة، وعرف أنها ليست من كتابته.|لكنه رأى فيها فرصة لإنهاء العداوة،|فقال للرسول إنها رسالته حقًا،|وأوصى الوالي بأن يحسن معاملة حاملها.
subtitles.en: Yahya immediately recognized the forgery.|Yet he saw a chance for peace|and told the envoy the letter was indeed his,|urging Abdullah to honor its bearer.

subtitles.ar: فرح عبد الله بهذا الجواب، وأعطى الرجل مئتي ألف درهم،|وعشرة خيول عربية، وصناديق من الثياب، وخدمًا وجواهر.|وأصبح اسم يحيى، الذي كان سببًا للخلاف، سببًا لتجدد المودة بين الرجلين.
subtitles.en: Delighted, Abdullah gave the man two hundred thousand dirhams,|ten Arabian horses, chests of clothes, servants and jewels.|The estranged men began to reconcile.

subtitles.ar: عاد الرجل إلى بغداد وهو لا يكاد يصدق ما حدث.|ذهب إلى يحيى، واعترف بما صنع،|وشكره على إنقاذه من العقوبة.|ثم عرض عليه شيئًا من الهدايا الكثيرة التي حصل عليها.
subtitles.en: Back in Baghdad, the astonished man|admitted his trick to Yahya,|thanked him for saving him from punishment,|and offered him part of his gifts.

subtitles.ar: ابتسم يحيى ورفض أن يأخذ شيئًا،|وقال إن الرجل كان سببًا في الصلح بين صديقين تفرقا.|ثم زاده من ماله وخيله مثل ما ناله،|فخرج الفقير بغنيمتين بدل واحدة.
subtitles.en: Yahya refused.|The visitor had brought peace between two estranged men, he said.|Yahya then matched the wealth and horses the man had received,|doubling his reward.

new_assets.name: horse
new_assets.description: The planned riding horse (same function as AN-084/085/086): 320 wide, back 235 above the feet, palettes white, bay, black; fields ph, amp, rear, headDown, headTurn, ears, tail swing, plus a returned back/saddle point. Here also drawn as head and neck only inside the hall door arch.
new_assets.implementation: Rounded box body with Ben-Day dots, four two-segment legs driven by walk() phase (gallop pose pair when amp > 1.4), neck as a tapered quad, head a rounded wedge, mane tufts as overlapping arcs, tail as a 3-point curve with swing(). Wrap with acting(). Clip to the arch for the door view.

new_assets.name: rideOn
new_assets.description: The planned front-facing person seated on a side-view mount: hips on the mount back point, one near leg hanging, inherits bob and rear, lurches on stops. Used for the envoy (S8) and the forger (S13, S17).
new_assets.implementation: rideOn(mountFn, mountP, personP): draw the mount, then the person clipped at the saddle line translated to the back point with a 2-frame lagged bob; near leg as one flat shape; lurch(t, stopT).

new_assets.name: scroll
new_assets.description: The planned small scroll extended with states this story needs: roll 0..1, lines 0..1 (draw-on), seal colour, broken seal, header slot for a portraitMedallion, and an enlarged insert size.
new_assets.implementation: Paper rect with two rolled-end capsules; wavy lines as sine polylines revealed by length; seal = disc with a darker ring; broken = two half discs falling with fallY.

new_assets.name: portraitMedallion
new_assets.description: A round portrait of any person head (r 34 to 80): yellow rim, paper ground with blue dots, the head and headwear of a given person pose clipped to the circle, so its eyes can gaze and it can nod. Used as the sign of each man's NAME on the letter and in the feud pictures.
new_assets.implementation: Clip circle; call person() with the given costume at a scale that puts the head centre on the circle centre; stroke the rim with the brush border. Fields: who (person pose), r, gaze, drop.

new_assets.name: rift
new_assets.description: The quarrel drawn as a red zigzag crack between two things: 8 segments, height 220 to 300, draw-on from the top (open 0..1), zip shut from the bottom (close 0..1), optional cobwebs at the top corners (age), alpha.
new_assets.implementation: Seeded zigzag polyline (K.rng) stroked red 10 px over black 16 px; reveal by segment count; closing = segments shorten toward the centre line; cobweb = 3 arcs and 4 spokes with draw-on.

new_assets.name: coinPile
new_assets.description: Planned coin mound with n growing and loose coins that fall and hop; with the counter it shows 200,000 dirhams.
new_assets.implementation: Seeded stack of yellow ellipses with black edges inside a mound outline; n reveals coins bottom to top; loose coins use fallY and rebound.

new_assets.name: treasureHoard (chest) and jewels (jewelBox)
new_assets.description: The planned chest with lid open 0..1 and contents cloth or coins, and the planned jewel casket with four gems.
new_assets.implementation: Box, arc lid rotating about the back edge, bands; cloth bolts as three rounded rects; gems as 6-point polygons with a white facet.

new_assets.name: quillInk, bindle, hourglass
new_assets.description: Three small props: quill and inkpot (new), planned bindle, planned hourglass.
new_assets.implementation: Flat shapes only; the quill follows handRW; the hourglass level is a kfn and its flip a 0.3 s rotation.

new_assets.name: goldGlow, inset circle
new_assets.description: Planned treasure light (rays and star glints, strength 0..1) and the planned round picture-in-picture with an iris, used once for the confession replay.
new_assets.implementation: goldGlow: tapering yellow rays plus halftone disc; inset: circular clip r 150 with a brush rim, iris by radius, inside draws the S3 writing pose at 30 % scale.

owner_questions: The punishment is softened to a picture: a stick in a box (S6) and a black silhouette arm with a raised stick that never falls (S9); nobody is hit on screen. Default: keep it softened.
From 116.56 the forger wears a yellow gift cloak over his patched robe (from the 'chests of clothes'), so he looks enriched in the last scenes. Default: yes.
Ten horses are shown as up to four whole horses plus heads in the door arch and a x10 tag, not ten full drawings. Default: yes.

The feud and the reconciliation are drawn as two portrait medallions with a red rift that zips shut under a small heart; the two men are never shown meeting, since the script does not say they met. Default: yes.
Yahya winks to camera at 99.28 while telling the envoy the letter is his (a comic addition showing he knows it is a lie told for peace). Default: keep the wink.

Invented English lettering: A POOR MAN OF IRAQ, GOVERNOR OF ARMENIA, VIZIER YAHYA, FORGED!, TO BAGHDAD, DAYS PASS..., NOT MY HAND!, IT IS MINE., HA HA!, 200,000 DIRHAMS, x10, BACK TO BAGHDAD, ME?, x2, THE END. Default: use all of them.
Armenia is suggested only by three snow-capped mountains behind the desert road and the label; no real architecture is attempted. Default: yes.
Yahya's true reply is drawn as a second scroll with a yellow seal (the script only says he told the envoy and urged the governor); it lets the audience see the answer travel. Default: yes.
implementation_notes: Start from Library/template. Word cues: use w(p, n) from timing.json; every cue in this plan gives the Arabic word and its start time on the final MP3 (timeline.md).

People: person() with costume presets and pal overrides only (villager, merchant as governor, vizier, bedouin, servant). Set LIFE.t = t each frame for auto blinks; add hand blinks where lid is set. Every figure always has a gaze target (look()/lookAt()).

Two halls from one set: palaceHall({variant:'palace', wall:'blue'}) for Armenia and wall:'ochre' with cushions for Baghdad. Take door, dais, throne and stool positions from the returned anchors; the numbers in this plan are the documented defaults (approximate, measure on the set).
Direction rule for the road: to Armenia = left to right, to Baghdad = right to left. Keep it in all three road scenes (S4, S8, S13) and in S17 (leaving to the left).
The recurring picture (two medallions + rift) appears in S2, S5, S10, S12, S15 in the same layout so the audience learns it once: Abdullah always on the left, Yahya always on the right.
The LATER card is at 72.62 (DAYS PASS...). Hide the cut from the road to the hall under the card midpoint with two camera keys 0.01 s apart.
Inserts (scroll close-ups in S3 and S10) are drawn in panel space over a dimmed scene, with the reader's eyes peeking over the top edge; do not zoom the world camera to 2.6.
Horses in the hall are drawn inside palaceHall outside(ctx), clipped by the door arch: head and neck only, each with its own nod phase. Never more than four whole horses on screen.

Sound: narration is the soundtrack. Effects only at 7.4 pop, 76.5 tick, 104.75 whoosh, 129.35 chime, 140.35 pop, 150.3 pop, 155.3 thud, 166.95 chime, 171.9 chime; SND master 0.6. No hoof sounds under speech.
Panel-only shake for FORGED! (21.56) and x2 (165.26); the caption panel never moves.
Subtitles: use the subtitles array as chunks_ar.txt / chunks_en.txt (| marks); text is verbatim from story/script.json.
Keep all faces and hands above world y 900 and inside the panel; counters and labels go in the upper band (y 120..420) and never over a face.
warnings: P6 is chunked in 3: the last Arabic chunk has 12 words (119.68 to 129.02); the English has only one short sentence for it, so it cannot be split further without mismatch. Check the Arabic font size fits three lines.
S10 runs 21.2 s in one room; it is carried by acting (freeze, decision, wink). If it feels static in the review, widen the camera change at 96.1.
The English translation is a condensed paraphrase of the Arabic (see SCRIPT note in the Markdown, section 8); nothing was changed.
horse and rideOn are planned by other stories but not in Library yet; this film needs them in three scenes. If they are late, S8/S13/S17 can fall back to walking figures leading horses by a rope.
Word times at phrase starts can include up to 0.4 s of silence (for example 18.44, 39.76, 60.6, 83.28, 105.04); check the onsets of those first words when keying the cuts.
